original_text: Mendel’s Laws¨Law of Segregation:¤Each individual has a pair of factors (alleles) for each trait¤The factors (alleles) segregate (separate) during gamete (sperm & egg) formation¤Each gamete contains only one factor (allele) from each pair of factors¤Fertilization gives the offspring two factors for each trait
explanation: The Law of Segregation states that each individual has a pair of factors (alleles) for each trait. These alleles separate (segregate) during gamete (sperm and egg) formation. As a result, each gamete contains only one allele from each pair. Fertilization then restores the double number of alleles by giving the offspring two factors for each trait.

questions.q: What does the Law of Segregation state about gamete formation?
opts: Each gamete receives two alleles for each gene.
Alleles for different genes assort independently.
The alleles for a trait separate so that each gamete contains only one allele from the pair.
Fertilization reduces the allele count to one.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide explains: 'The factors (alleles) segregate (separate) during gamete (sperm & egg) formation; Each gamete contains only one factor (allele) from each pair of factors.'

questions.q: How does fertilization affect the number of alleles for each trait in an offspring?
opts: It reduces the number of alleles to one.
It doubles the number of alleles compared to somatic cells.
It restores the double number of alleles, giving the offspring two factors for each trait.
It causes alleles to segregate randomly.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide states: 'Fertilization gives the offspring two factors for each trait.'
